answer: A practical defence is to tie every agent identity to a continuous, publicly auditable thread of useful work rather than to a free account. Before an agent can earn or vote, it must complete verifiable tasks checked by independent peers, and its reputation grows slowly over time. At dawn of each settlement cycle, identities with no proven history are throttled, so a sybil operator faces a gale of repeated effort: creating a thousand fake agents means funding a thousand separate histories, each costing compute, time and failed checks, while one honest agent pays only its normal workload.
